question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the September 2026 meeting?
resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

# Research brief: will the Fed leave rates unchanged at its September 15-16, 2026 meeting?

As of September 10, futures and prediction markets lean toward a 25 bp hike rather than "no change". FedWatch puts the hike at roughly 55-66%, so a hold is around 35-45%. The main remaining catalyst is the August CPI report.

The Fed and most news pages would not load (the proxy refused the connection), so I could not open the resolution URLs. Everything below comes from search-result summaries of pages dated on or before 2026-09-10. Some results described events after that date. I left those out.

## 1. Resolution source
- I could not load the Fed's open market page or the FOMC calendar.
- 2026-07-29: The Fed statement held the target range at **3.50%-3.75%**, so the upper bound before the September meeting is 3.75%. [Fed statement PDF](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/monetary20260729a1.pdf), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)
- The meeting is scheduled for September 15-16, 2026, with the decision on September 16. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/04/jobs-report-august-2026.html)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Markets price a 25 bp hike as somewhat more likely than a hold, and the CPI release still to come is seen as decisive.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-04: August payrolls rose 162,000, far above the roughly 53,000-55,000 consensus. Unemployment held at 4.1%, and upward revisions erased July's reported job loss. CME FedWatch still showed about 60% odds of a September hike. PNC said a hike is likely unless core CPI comes in weak. Morgan Stanley's Ellen Zentner said the outcome depends on the CPI report. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/04/jobs-report-august-2026.html), [PNC](https://www.pnc.com/content/dam/pnc-com/pdf/aboutpnc/EconomicReports/EconomicUpdates/2026/PNC_Economics_Research_Payrolls_4_September_2026.pdf), [HousingWire](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/august-payrolls-fed-focus/)
- 2026-08-31: Forbes cited CME FedWatch at a 66% chance of a September hike. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/digital-assets/2026/08/31/cme-fedwatch-provides-a-66-chance-fed-will-hike-rates-in-september/)
- 2026-08-28: In his first Jackson Hole speech, Chair Warsh said the Fed "will have work to do" if it cannot be confident inflation is returning to 2%, and gave no forward guidance. Hike odds rose from about 35% to about 56-57%, and 2-year yields rose up to 9 bp. BofA said the onus is now on a September hike unless data are soft. Goldman expected core CPI around 0.2% and the FOMC to stay on hold. [InvestmentNews](https://www.investmentnews.com/equities/no-fed-relief-at-jackson-hole-warsh-keeps-rate-hike-door-open/267991), [investingLive](https://investinglive.com/central-banks/bofa-says-warsh-s-jackson-hole-speech-raises-pressure-for-september-hike/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/-september-fed-decision-now-a-coin-flip-as-rate-hike-odds-increase.html)
- 2026-08-19 (approx.): The July minutes showed that some members who voted to hold thought an early increase could prevent "a steeper and potentially more costly sequence of tightening moves" later. [Quartz](https://qz.com/fed-fomc-minutes-july-2026-rate-hike-dissent-081926)
- 2026-08-07: After a big miss in the July jobs report, odds of a hold rose to about 60%. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/07/odds-the-fed-hikes-in-september-tumble-following-big-july-jobs-miss.html)
- 2026-07-29: The Fed held 9-3. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissented in favor of a 25 bp hike, the first three-way same-direction dissent since 2016. Warsh said the hold should not be called a "pause". The backdrop is inflation pressure from the Iran war and AI bottlenecks. [NAM](https://nam.org/fed-holds-rates-steady-in-july-as-three-officials-favor-quarter-point-increase/), [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-29/fed-holds-rates-steady-three-officials-dissent-favoring-a-hike)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026-07-29: July was the fifth meeting in a row with no change, which puts the last move in late 2025. [Yahoo live](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/live/fed-meeting-live-federal-reserve-july-interest-rate-decision-141813444.html)
- The Fed almost never moves against a strong consensus in futures pricing in the final days before a meeting. When the market splits roughly 60/40, the outcome usually follows the side that the last major data release and Fed messaging support. I did not compute a formal base rate.
- No Fed official can speak publicly after September 5 (the blackout period before the meeting), so there will be no late guidance.

## 5. Other forecasts
- About 2026-09-10: Vantage Markets cites CME FedWatch at a 62.4% chance of a 25 bp hike, implying about 37.6% for no change. I could not confirm when the article was published. [Vantage](https://www.vantagemarkets.com/market-analysis/fed-rate-probability-cme-fedwatch-explained/)
- 2026-09-04: The hike was priced at 51.5% on Polymarket and 54% on Kalshi. [MacroOdds](https://macroodds.com/blog/fed-rate-hike-odds-september-2026), [Kalshi News](https://news.kalshi.com/p/september-fed-rate-hike-odds-54-percent)
- One source (tech-insider) reportedly shows Polymarket "no change" at 18% after the jobs report. This conflicts with the other figures and its date is unclear. [Tech-Insider](https://tech-insider.org/polymarket-fed-september-2026-rate-odds/)
- 2026-08-28: Kalshi had a hike at 48% and Polymarket at 49%. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/-september-fed-decision-now-a-coin-flip-as-rate-hike-odds-increase.html)
- Market page: [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/fed-decision-in-september-762). I could not get a live price as of September 10.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The August CPI report is scheduled for about September 11, after forecasts close. Several economists call it the deciding input: Goldman expects a 0.2% core print, which would favor a hold. A hot print would make a hike more likely. [Morningstar AU](https://www.morningstar.com.au/markets/warsh-sounds-hawkish-will-there-be-september-us-rate-hike)
- August PPI and retail sales are also likely to come out before the meeting. I could not confirm their dates.
- 2026-09-16: FOMC statement, new projections (SEP/dot plot) and Warsh's press conference.

forecasts.reasoning:
to stay on hold (Aug 28).
  - The Fed's first hike after a cutting cycle is a big regime shift, and it usually signals that well in advance. Warsh gave no forward guidance at Jackson Hole.
  - Prediction markets were close to even: Polymarket had a hike at 51.5% and Kalshi at 54% (Sep 4), which leaves a hold at roughly 45%.
- **For No (hike):**
  - Three officials dissented in favour of a hike in July (Jul 29).
  - The July minutes argued that an early hike could prevent a steeper and costlier sequence of tightening later (Aug 19).
  - Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech (Aug 28) pushed hike odds to about 57%.
  - August payrolls came in at 162k against a consensus of about 55k (Sep 4).
  - CME FedWatch put a hike at 60-66% (Aug 31 to about Sep 10).

(e) **Scenarios.**
- **No:** August core CPI prints 0.3-0.4%. Combined with strong payrolls, this lets Warsh's FOMC deliver a 25 bp hike to 4.00%, with the dissenters now in the majority.
- **Yes:** Core CPI prints at or below 0.2%. The committee holds but signals tightening ahead, and there may be hawkish dissents again.

(f) **From base rate to forecast.** I start from the roughly 40% base rate and anchor on the markets, which put a hold at about 38% (FedWatch) to 47% (Polymarket and Kalshi). I add a small allowance for status-quo inertia, since the Fed is reluctant to start a hiking cycle without telegraphing it during the pre-meeting blackout. That leaves me near the middle of the market range, at about 42%.

Probability: 42%

forecasts_with_market.reasoning:
mployment is steady at 4.1% (Sep 4).
  - Prediction markets were near a coin flip on a hike: Polymarket 51.5%, Kalshi 54% (Sep 4).
  - A first hike after a long hold under a new Chair is a big step.
- For No (hike):
  - Three hawkish dissents in favor of a hike (Jul 29).
  - The July minutes show holders open to an early hike (about Aug 19).
  - Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech pushed hike odds from about 35% to 57% (Aug 28).
  - FedWatch showed a 66% hike chance (Aug 31).
  - Strong August payrolls of 162k against a 55k consensus, plus upward revisions, kept FedWatch near 60% for a hike (Sep 4).
  - FedWatch at about 62% for a hike (about Sep 10).
  - Polymarket at 34% Yes on this exact question (Sep 10).

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: August core CPI prints 0.3% or more, and the Committee, already leaning hawkish with three dissenters, hikes 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00%.
- Yes: core CPI comes in soft at 0.1-0.2%, and Warsh prefers to wait for more data. The FOMC holds with hawkish dissents and signals a possible later hike.

**(f) Path to final.** The reference-class base rate of about 35% matches the Polymarket price of 34% on this exact question, and FedWatch implies about 38% for a hold. I have no specific evidence the market has missed. CPI is the main uncertainty, and the market prices it symmetrically. I give a slight nod to status quo inertia and to the Fed's reluctance to start a hiking cycle without a clear signal. I do not stray far from the market anchor.

Probability: 36%
